SUBJF,CT:  Conditional  Use Permit  (CUP  24-32)

PROJECT  PROPOSAL/REQUEST:  Request  for approval  of a Conditional  Use Permit  to allow
the installation  of a roof-mounted  solar photovoltaic  (PV)  system  consisting  of 327 panels  on an
existing multi-tenant  commercial  building.

BACKGROUND:

Project  Overview

*  General  Plan Designation:  Commercial

*  Hollydale  Village  Specific  Plan (Hollydale  Mixed  Use-3)

@  Project  Location:  5720 Imperial  Highway

*  Assessor's  Parcel  Number(s):  6234-005-010  and 6234-005-015

*  Site Characteristics:  The subject  site is a triangularly  shaped  lot that measures  approximately
  72,642  square  feet  (1.67  acres)  and is comprised  of two  separate  parcels  with  two  street
  frontages.  The primary  frontage  is along  Garfield  Avenue,  and the secondary  (side)  frontage
  is along  Imperial  Highway.  The site is currently  developed  with  a multi-tenant  commercial
  building,  a restaurant  pad, and surface-level  parking  lot: and is occupied  with  retail,  restaurant,
  and office  uses.

*  Surroundings:  Surrounding  properties  include  the  Southern  Pacific  railroad  track  directly
  adjacent  to the  west,  an auto body  collision  center  across  Imperial  Highway  to the north,  a
  "Carl's  Jr." restaurant  and "SOLA"  multi-family  residential  development  to the east and south
  of the subject  site, across Garfield  Avenue.

*  ProjectDescription:Theproposalisforanewinstallationofaroof-mountedsolarphotovoltaic
  (PV)  system  consisting  of 327 panels  on an existing  multi-tenant  commercial  building.  No
  additional  improvements  are proposed  as part of the project.

*  Property  Owner:  Southgate  Center  Associates  LLC

*  Derek  Robert,  Solirvine  LLC

•  Municipal Code Requirements for Conditional Use Permit (CUP): Pursuant to the City of
  South Gate Hollydale Village Specific Plan (HVSP) Section 4.4 Urban Mixed-Use Zone, Table
  4-2: Allowed Land Use for Urban Mixed-Use Zones, a CUP is required for building-mounted
  renewable energy systems.

•  Required Findings for a Conditional Use Permit: Pursuant to SGMC Chapter 11.52.030, before
  a conditional use permit may be granted, the Planning Commission shall make all of the
  following findings, as applicable to the property:

  a. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and
  purpose of this title or the City’s general plan.

  b. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible
  with the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  c. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or
  to the character or function of the neighborhood.

ANALYSIS:

Description of Site Improvements

The proposed project involves the new installation of a solar photovoltaic (PV) system consisting
of 327 panels manufactured by Suzhou Talesun Solar Technologies, to be mounted on the roof of
on an existing 17,890 square foot multi-tenant commercial building; and two (2) inverters, 166
optimizers and associated mechanical equipment improvements to be located within an existing
ground-level electrical room. Such improvements will consist of an AC disconnect, transformer,
and utility meter for energy metering. The project system size consists of a 132.435 kw, Standard
Test Conditions (STC) DC rating and 120.388 kw, California Energy Commission (CEC) AC
rating.

Pursuant to the HVSP, renewable energy systems shall comply with SGMC Chapter 11.40.180
and the applicable development standards detailed in the table below:

As proposed, the PV system is in compliance with setback and height requirements, however,
exceeds the maximum allowable (30 percent) coverage of roof surface. The existing building is
set back 15 feet from Garfield Avenue, 80 feet from Imperial Hwy; and 5 feet from the interior
property line which abuts the railroad track. Therefore, the PV system complies with all the setback
requirements. Additionally, the height requirement has been met. There are three (3) types of
panels proposed, which are as follows: the (1)“Tilt Up Portrait” and (2)“Tilt Up Landscape” panels
which will have an overall heigh of 10 inches from base to the top of panel; and will be located
toward the west side of the building and will not exceed the height of the existing 2’-10” building
parapet; and the (3)“6up” panel which will have an overall height of 4’-6” from base to the top of
panel all located toward the east side of the building adjacent to the existing 7 feet parapet. Per
Los Angeles County Office of the Assessors and City records the existing building measures
approximately 17,890 square feet and the PV system will cover 6,736 square feet, equaling
approximately 38 percent of the exiting roof area. The proposed PV system propose coverage is
38 percent, which can be permitted with the approval of the CUP.

Compatibility

Overall, the existing site is a highly utilized multi-tenant commercial site that would benefit from
the installation of the proposed PV system. The state agencies have already set renewable energy
targets, and this project will help to achieve those targets in the set time frame. Additionally,
conditions of approval are recommended to ensure that exterior features of the site are well
maintained, such as landscaping and re-painting of the west-facing facade along the railroad tracks.

Conditional Use Permit Analysis

In granting approval of a CUP to allow the new installation of a solar panel system consisting of
327 modules on the roof of an existing multi-tenant commercial building, the Planning
Commission shall make all of the following findings, as applicable to the property:

A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and
  purpose of this title or the City’s general plan. The proposed project will not create new
  uses or increase the existing building areas of the site. Therefore, the site will remain
  unchanged and will be continuing to be utilized as a multi-tenant commercial site. Goal 7 of
  the Green City Element is to mitigate against and adapt to climate change. The proposed
  project aligns directly with such goal in that it involves the installation of a renewable energy
  system. Therefore, the granting of the CUP for the proposed project will not adversely affect
  the intent and purpose of the Zoning Code or the General Plan.

B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible
  with the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone. Pursuant to the City of South
  Gate Hollydale Village Specific Plan (HVSP) Section 4.4 Urban Mixed-Use Zone, Table 4-2:
  Allowed Land Use for Urban Mixed-Use Zones, a CUP is required for building-mounted
  Renewable Energy System land use type. As proposed, the project complies with the applicable
  setbacks and height requirements but exceeds the allowable (30 percent) roof surface
  coverage. However pursuant to Chapter 11.40.180(B)(3), additional area coverage may be

  permitted through a CUP approval. Staff has determined that with the recommended
  conditions of approval, the granting of the CUP will be compatible with the existing and future
  land uses of the HMU3 zone.

C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or
  to the character or function of the neighborhood. The subject site is currently developed
  with a multi-tenant commercial building occupied with uses such as retail, restaurant, and
  offices and an existing off-street parking lot. The proposed solar panel system will be mounted
  on the roof the building and screened from public view. Therefore, the granting of the CUP,
  as conditioned, would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the
  character or function of the neighborhood.

Conclusion

Based on the above analysis, the staff has determined that with the recommended conditions of
approval, the proposed project complies with the SGMC, and all the required findings in support
of Conditional Use Permit.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:

In accordance with the criteria and authority contained in the California Environmental Quality
Act (CEQA), staff has conducted the appropriate environmental analysis and based on that
assessment, the City has determined the project to be Categorically Exempt by Article 19 Section
15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities), in that the project involves no expansion to an existing
commercial building and thereby is exempt from CEQA. No further environmental assessment is
required.

COMMENTS FROM OTHER DEPARTMENTS:

Staff routed the project for comments to several City Departments including the Public Works,
Code Enforcement, and the Building & Safety Division. The Building & Safety Division and Code
Enforcement provided conditions (attached). If the project is approved, the comments received
from all departments would be incorporated as conditions of approval.

RECOMMENDATION:

Based on the evidence presented, Staff recommends that the Planning Commission find that the
project is categorically exempt from the CEQA under Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing
Facilities”, make the required findings and requirements set forth in the South Gate Municipal
Code, and approve the application for Conditional Use Permit (CUP 24-32) subject to the
proposed conditions of approval and/or other conditions that the Planning Commission may wish
to impose.
